title: Ideal subsheaves on a ringed site and extension of ideals
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. An ideal subsheaf $I\subset R$ consists of an ideal $I(U)\subset R(U)$ for every object $U$, preserved by restriction, with membership local on covering sieves. Its underlying module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] has sections $I(U)$ and the inherited restriction and scalar action, with its canonical inclusion into the ring module; finite type means finite type of this module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. For $\varphi:R\to B$ a ring-sheaf homomorphism, define $IB$ to be the unique ideal subsheaf whose sections locally lie in the ideals generated by the images of sections of $I$. Define the predicate that the induced map $R/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism by its equivalent local criteria: $\varphi(a)\in IB(U)$ if and only if $a\in I(U)$; and each $b\in B(U)$ admits on a covering sieve local lifts $a\in R(V)$ modulo $IB(V)$. Regard the commutative ring sheaf as a ring sheaf by forgetting commutativity.
